newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil profits up on higher oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Statoil profits up on higher oil prices.

text.p: Norwegian state energy company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday firm oil prices combined with high and stable crude oil production lifted operating profits nearly 20 percent in the first nine months of the year.
The company booked an operating result of 13.1 billion crowns in the period to September 30 compared with 11 billion crowns a year ago.

"In addition, the group's refineries achieved better results than in the first nine months 1995. Oil trading operations also reported good earnings," a Statoil statement said. "Profits from petrochemicals showed a clear decline from last year."

Statoil forecast oil prices to remain near current levels as a result of low stocks and good demand. Refining and petrochemical margins were unlikely to change significantly in the short term, while the contraction in retailing margins would probably persist through the fourth quarter, it said.
"The overall effect is expected to be an operating profit for the fourth quarter on a par with the results from the third quarter."

Nine-month profits before tax were stable at 12.3 billion crowns against 12.4 billion crowns, but profits after tax dipped due to higher tax payments from increased offshore activities. Net profits anounted to 3.9 billion crowns versus 4.5 billion crowns.

Average production equity increased to 463,000 barrels per day (bpd) compared with 415,000 bpd in the first nine months 1995 as start up of Norway's Heidrun, Yme and Troll fields together with international output from the wholly-owned Aran subsidiary, more than compensated for a decline at the Statfjord complex.
Daily gas sales totalled 18.5 billion cubic metres versus 11.6 billion cubic metres in the same period last year.
No significant changes were expected in Statoil's oil and gas production during the remainder of 1996, the company said.
